newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Icatu sees Brazil 97/98 coffee crop of 24 mln bags.
newsitem.headline: Icatu sees Brazil 97/98 coffee crop of 24 mln bags.

text.p: Brazil's 1997/98 coffee harvest may drop to 24 million 60-kg bags after an upwardly revised 27.65 million in 1996/97, said Santos exporter Icatu/Sumatra.
"Taking into account the bi-annual low cycle, we will be glad if we reach an overall harvest of about 24 million bags (in the 1997/98 harvest)," Icatu/Sumatra said in a statement.

Precise estimates of the 1997/98 crop could be delayed until February because some coffee-growing regions had up to five flowerings, a factor which could also reduce the overall quality expectation, it said.
The exporter said it had decided to upwardly revise its previous 1996/97 harvest forecast of 26 million bags based on recent heavy exports and good local supply.
This was due mainly to an increase in production of Group 1 coffee and better than expected output in the south of Minas, which now is seen to have reached 8.75 million bags.
Icatu said exports of green and soluble coffee would total 15 million bags in 1996 and the government would have to increase its monthly sales of stocks in 1997 to maintain that rhythm.
"Nevertheless, we preview a steady and constant decrease of exports on a monthly basis from January onwards," it added.
The government has sold 968,302 bags to date in 1996 out of the 1,512,691 it made available from its stocks.
